I trust no one. Assume everyone will betray you and you will never be disappointed.|Tobias Beckett to Han Solo|}} '''Tobias Beckett''' was a [[human]] [[Gender|male]] professional [[thief]] and [[gunslinger]] [[Homeworld|native]] to [[Glee Anselm]] who worked for the [[Crimson Dawn]] crime syndicate during the early [[Imperial Era|reign]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. Beckett organized a [[Beckett's gang|crew]] to take part in his heists and other jobs, including his lover, [[Val]], and [[Rio Durant]]. On one job for the syndicate, he [[Death|killed]] the prominent [[bounty hunter]] [[Aurra Sing]]. On a [[Heist on Vandor|failed job]] to steal Imperial [[coaxium]] on behalf of Crimson Dawn, Beckett recruited [[Han Solo]] and [[Chewbacca]] to his gang, though Val and Durant were killed. With the help of Solo, who Beckett took into his mentorship, Beckett pivoted to instead [[Raid on Kessel|steal]] the needed coaxium from [[Kessel]], a plan that succeeded. However, when Solo decided to betray Crimson Dawn and give the [[hypermatter]] to the [[Cloud-Riders]], Beckett in turn betrayed Solo. This resulted in a [[Showdown on Savareen|standoff]] between the two, in which Solo fatally shot his mentor. ==Biography== ===Early life=== {{Quote|You're Tobias Beckett. You killed Aurra Sing."
"Pushed her. Pretty sure the fall killed her.|Lando Calrissian and Tobias Beckett|}} Tobias Beckett was [[Reproduction|born]] on the [[planet]] [[Glee Anselm]]. Around [[13 BBY]], he met the [[bounty hunter]] [[Aurra Sing]] and pushed her to her [[death]]. Sing's death was later recalled by Beckett while talking with [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]], though Beckett claimed that he just pushed Sing and that it was the fall that killed her. ===Cato Neimoidia heist=== Beckett's lover [[Val]] found the logbook that would become known as the ''[[Smuggler's Guide]]'' previously owned by [[Qi'ra]] in the crate the gang stole from the freight platform in [[Zarra]] on [[Cato Neimoidia]]. After spending a brief time investigating on the planet Cato Neimoidia, Beckett and [[Beckett's gang|his gang]], consisting of Val and [[Rio Durant]], formulated a plan to rob a [[20-T Railcrawler conveyex transport|Railcrawler conveyex]] suspected of carrying [[Crimson Dawn]] cargo. The plan involved intercepting the conveyex before it reached [[Tarko-se]].''[[Star Wars: Smuggler's Guide]]'' ===Hovun IV heist=== [[File:BeckettGangHovunIV-Beckett1.jpg|thumb|left|252px|Beckett and his gang on Hovun IV]] Beckett and his gang went to [[Hovun IV]] on a mission for Crimson Dawn. There, Beckett, posing as a [[death priest]], pretended to [[Force choke]] Rio Durant in order to scare several [[sabacc]] players away from Durant's game. After the players left, Beckett congratulated Durant on pulling off the trick. Beckett asked [[Val]] if she placed the tracker on [[Dvorad]], and she said she did. Beckett and his gang went to the dock to find Dvorad in order to [[Heist on Hovun IV|steal]] [[identichip]]s. Beckett was able to jump onto [[Dvorad's speeder]], punched him, and made it to [[Dvorad's ship]]. Beckett and his gang were held at gunpoint by Dvorad and his [[Starship|ship]] until a [[Unidentified Hovun IV creature|creature]] attacked. As his gang and Dvorad fought the creature, Beckett boarded the ship and fought his way past Dvorad's guards. Aboard, Beckett was able to find the the chips and make his way back to Val and Durant in order to make their escape before the creature pulled Dvorad's ship into the depths. As they left, Beckett shot down Durant's idea about keeping some of the chips for themselves instead of giving all of them to Crimson Dawn's leader, [[Dryden Vos]]. Beckett then summoned the ''[[Rampart]]'' and left Hovun IV. [[File:EnfysAndBeckett-Beckett1.jpg|thumb|right|238px|Beckett confronted by Nest and several of her Cloud-Riders]] As the ''Rampart'' made its way to [[Munt Ontdal]], Beckett tried to think of a way to leave Crimson Dawn. After landing on Munt Ontdal, Beckett took his [[speeder]] to meet with Vos. However, he came under attack by several [[knife]]-wielding [[Thief|thieves]]. Beckett, seeing it as as a setup, tried to escape but was knocked out by [[Enfys Nest]], leader of the [[Cloud-Riders]]. Despite knowing Vos would arrive shortly, Beckett was told by Val that Nest faked the mission. Beckett, to prevent Nest from getting the chips, blew them and the ''Rampart'' up. Despite wanting to finish Nest off, Beckett was convinced to let them go for the [[Standard day|day]]. As Beckett and his gang were confronted by several [[stormtrooper]]s, he lied to them by saying that the explosion was caused by [[black market]] radioactive [[fuel]]. Beckett, Val, and Durant then decided to resume their [[death]] [[priest]] scheme. ===Undercover on Mimban=== [[File:BeckettImperial-SoloOMG.png|thumb|left|200px|Beckett disguised as an Imperial officer on Mimban]] Sometime later, Beckett, Durant, and Val, traveled to [[Mimban]], where the [[Galactic Empire]] was engaged in a [[Mimban Campaign|campaign]] with the [[Mimbanese Liberation Army]]. Beckett disguised himself as a [[captain]] of the [[Imperial Army]] while the others disguised themselves as [[Imperial Army]] [[Imperial Army trooper|soldiers]] ("[[Swamp trooper|mudtrooper]]" variants) . At some point during a battle, Beckett asked who was in charge, since [[Staz|their]] [[commanding officer]] had recently perished. [[Han Solo]], a [[Swamp trooper|mudtrooper]] with the [[224th Imperial Armored Division]], informed Beckett that he was in fact the ranking [[officer]], which amused his cohorts. Beckett led the Imperials successfully through the battle. Later, while observing an [[Y-45 armored transport hauler|AT-hauler]], he was approached by the young Solo, who wanted to join their crew. However, when Solo pressed the point by threatening to expose Beckett as an impostor, Beckett used his phony rank to have Solo [[Prisoner|locked up]] for desertion. Solo was put in a chamber, where he was to be fed to the [[Wookiee]] [[Chewbacca]]. Solo ultimately was able to escape with Chewbacca. Beckett left with his crew, stealing the AT-hauler they observed earlier, but while in mid-takeoff they found Solo and Chewbacca running towards them, waving for them to let them onto the ship. Beckett ordered Durant to lower the hauler to let Solo and Chewbacca board. ===Vandor heist=== Beckett was instructed to retrieve a crate of [[coaxium]] from a 20-T Railcrawler conveyex transport on the planet [[Vandor]]; he went on this [[Heist on Vandor|mission]] with Val, Durant, Solo and Chewbacca. [[File:DL44rifle-pistol.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Beckett converting his DL-44 rifle into a pistol before giving it to Solo.]] Upon arriving at Vandor, the crew ate [[Foodstuff|dinner]] over a campfire and had a brief conversation about Solo's and Chewbacca's motivation for participating in the mission. Solo simply stated that there was [[Qi'ra|someone]] he left on [[Corellia]] and that he wanted to return there to free her from her horrible life there. Val stated that everyone needed someone, even Beckett. Beckett began deconstructing one of his [[blaster]]s and [[Han's heavy blaster pistol|chucked]] it to Solo. In the morning, Beckett, Val and Solo observed the [[transport]] carrying the coaxium as well as some patrolling [[11-3K viper probe droid|viper droids]], while discussing the plan for the heist. The [[ICC-5537|conveyex]] was moving towards a bridge over a ravine. The plan was for Val to place explosives on the supports of the bridge. The other members of the crew were to board the [[Train|conveyex]] and attach cables from the carriage which contained the coaxium to their [[Y-45 armored transport hauler|ship]]. Then, as the conveyex neared the bridge, Val was to destroy the bridge while the crew disconnected the coaxium carriage from the rest of the conveyex, allowing the ship to lift the target carriage away while the rest of the conveyex fell to the bottom of the ravine. Val noted that if the [[Viper probe droid|viper droids]] were alerted, the heist would become much more difficult, prompting Solo to also survey the [[Probe droid|viper droids]]. [[File:The_Train_Job.png|thumb|left|300px|Beckett's ship above the conveyex]] Soon the heist began. Val went further up the track to place [[thermal detonator]]s, Durant flew their ship over the transport, and Beckett, Solo and Chewbacca leapt aboard the transport. They opened up a hatch and gazed upon the coaxium inside, enough to power a whole [[fleet]]. A fight ensued with [[range trooper]]s aboard the transport, but Chewbacca disconnected the [[trooper]]s' portion of the conveyex, leaving them behind as the rest of the conveyex moved onwards. The crew then connected four cables from their ship to the last carriage of the conveyex in order to lift it. The heist did not proceed smoothly, however, as Val spotted the Cloud-Riders, led by Nest, moving towards the conveyex. One Cloud-Rider boarded the crew's ship and had a brief firefight with Durant, who was gravely injured, diminishing his ability to [[pilot]] the ship. Val was surrounded by a swarm of viper droids. She told Beckett over the comm how much she loved him, and detonated the explosives while still near them. Solo took Durant's place as pilot and tried carrying the shipment with only one cable attached to the carriage. Nest and the Cloud-Riders had cut off the other three and replaced them with their own. Shortly, Durant perished too. Chewbacca uncoupled the carriage from the others so that they could lift the shipment off the tracks. Solo and the Cloud-Riders had to eventually lift the shipment, for they were running out of track. Both tried to take the shipment with them but failed as they were both pulling opposite directions. As both Solo and the Cloud-Riders neared a [[mountain]], Solo detached the shipment of coaxium, fearing a crash. The Cloud-Riders did so as well. The coaxium was lost. After they landed, Beckett made tombstones in remembrance of his fallen comrades. [[File:SoloBeckettAndVos-Solo.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Han and Beckett promising to retrieve unrefined coaxium from Kessel]] He reported to Vos and was able to avoid execution by promising to retrieve unrefined coaxium from [[Kessel]]. Beckett had to make room for Qi'ra on his crew in accordance with Vos' wishes. ===Mission to Kessel=== {{Quote|This is a precision job. Thermal vault will be on the lowest level. Down where it's warm. The only way we're going to pull this off is if everybody plays their part. Stick to the plan. Do not improvise… All right people, time to shine.|Tobias Beckett to his crew|}} [[File:HanBeckettChewieFalcon-MF16-OMG.png|thumb|left|300px|On the way to Kessel, Beckett warned Han not to trust Qi'ra.]] Taken to Kessel by Calrissian and [[L3-37]] on the ''[[Millennium Falcon]]'', Beckett, posing as a guard named Tuul, successfully [[Raid on Kessel|obtained]] the necessary amount of coaxium and traveled with his accomplices to [[Savareen]] so the unstable material could be refined and they could rendezvous with Vos. During the mission, Beckett posed as a guard for Qi'ra, directing the fake captives, Solo and Chewie, out of the ''Falcon''. He later followed Qi'ra, L3, [[Quay Tolsite]], a [[Pyke]] who administered the [[Pyke Syndicate]]'s [[Spice mines of Kessel|operations]] on Kessel, and his guards. While Qi'ra went into another room to negotiate with Tolsite, Beckett took out the guards, then watched Qi'ra fight Tolsite. After a moment of unnerving silence from the room, he opened the door, only to be astonished to see Tolsite lying on the floor with Qi'ra walking out of the room telling him that Vos had taught her [[Teräs Käsi]]. Once they got to the consoles to help Solo get to the vault of coaxium, L3 freed some [[Slavery|slave]] [[droid]]s, who also freed the other slaves in the [[Mining|mine]]. The slaves rebelled against the guards, allowing Beckett and the others to escape aboard the ''Millennium Falcon''. ===Refinery on Savareen and death=== {{Quote|I hope you're paying attention, because I'm about to tell you the most—''"
"''Beckett…''"
"''No. You made the smart move, kid. For once. I would've killed you.|Han and Beckett, the latter praising his killer in his final moments|''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition]]''}} [[File:Beckett_and_Chewie.png|thumb|right|220px|Beckett taking Chewbacca as prisoner]] On Savareen, Beckett showed his true colors to Solo, Qi'ra, and Chewbacca. After Solo had told Beckett their plan, Beckett reported to Vos. When they met Vos, Vos surprised the team by announcing that the coaxium was fake, which he knew because of his "inside man," whom Solo assumed to be Qi'ra but was indeed Beckett. He had informed Vos of Solo's plan to sell the real shipment to the Cloud-Riders, a rebellion group led by Nest. Solo announced that he anticipated Beckett's deception—the coaxium they were holding was real. [[File:Toby_gonna_die.png|thumb|left|245px|Beckett dies in Han Solo's arms.]] Beckett betrayed the three and abandoned Vos. He attempted to take the coaxium for himself, but as he explained his motives, he was shot by Solo. Before passing away, Beckett praised Solo for his actions in addition to revealing that he actually planned to return to Glee Anselm and learn to play the [[valachord]]. ===Legacy=== {{Quote|So what's your point?''"
"''That you're a little too—''"
"''Trusting? Maybe. But you're not exactly the first father figure of mine to think that.|Solo to his "father," recalling lessons learned from Beckett|[[Han Solo & Chewbacca 10|''Han Solo & Chewbacca'' 10]]}} Immediately after Solo left the ''First Light'', before he killed Beckett, Qi'ra reported Vos' death to [[Maul]], the [[Zabrak]] former [[Sith Lord]] who led Crimson Dawn from behind the shadows, and blamed Beckett for Vos' death, unaware that Beckett had been killed by the man she loved. Enraged, before ordering her to go to [[Dathomir]] so they could work more closely, Maul promised that he would think what to do with the traitorous Beckett, unaware that Beckett was no longer alive. After reuniting with Calrissian and winning the ''Millennium Falcon'' as his own in a game of sabacc, Solo recalled Beckett having spoken about a job for a big-shot gangster on [[Tatooine]]. For the next several [[Standard year|years]], Solo and Chewbacca found themselves in the employ of that gangster, [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure]] of the [[Hutt Clan]], though Solo never forgot the lessons and betrayals of his late mentor. Memories of their final encounter on Savareen in particular came back to Solo during a [[Heist on Corellia|job]] on Corellia, when he encountered a [[Ovan|man]] who claimed to be his [[Parent|father]]. Now knowing that trust was a valuable commodity, Solo remained wary of the man's intentions.[[Han Solo & Chewbacca 2|''Han Solo & Chewbacca'' 2]] ==Personality and traits== Beckett was a [[human]] who became a professional [[thief]] and a skilled [[gunslinger]]. Beckett was a survivor who quietly worked out angles that enabled him to come out ahead. Although he betrayed Han and Chewbacca, he genuinely cared for Val and Rio. Beckett was great at manipulating people and improvising during tough situations, such as during the Mimban Campaign, Beckett managed to convince several mudtroopers that he was the "captain" after Solo pointed it out and showed remarkable leadership skills that lead to the Imperial victory. ==Skills and abilities== Beckett was able to wield blasters in combat, utilizing two to eliminate a number of foes on Mimban. Beckett was a skilled gunslinger with incredible accuracy and was an extremely fast quick draw as he quickly killed many Mimbans soldiers, several [[Pyke sentinel]]s, and two of Vos' guards in a quick sensation. Although proficient in [[Unarmed combat|hand-to-hand combat]], Beckett was no match for Enfys Nest as seen during the Vandor heist. Beckett was also a capable leader. ==Equipment== Beckett carried many [[blaster]]s, including the [[RSKF-44 heavy blaster]] [[holster]]ed on his right side and [[DG-29 heavy blaster pistol]] holstered on his left side. He also owned a collapsible blade/[[fusioncutter]] and a [[DL-44 heavy blaster pistol]], which he gave [[Han's heavy blaster pistol|it]] to Solo. Beckett's DL-44 could also be reconfigured into a [[blaster rifle]]. On the Falcon, Beckett also had a [[A280-CFE convertible heavy blaster pistol]] in a [[backpack]] and spare RSKF-44 and DG-29 both had a black coloration. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|I play a guy named Beckett, who's kind of a criminal and a mentor to Han.|Woody Harrelson, on Tobias Beckett|{{WebCite|url=http://www.nbc.com/the-tonight-show/video/woody-harrelson-joined-star-wars-as-a-criminal-and-got-arrested/3489591|text=Woody Harrelson Joined Star Wars as a Criminal and Got Arrested|date=2017-03-22|archivedate=20220216200903}}}} [[File:Woody_Harrelson.jpg|thumb|Woody Harrelson]] Tobias Beckett appears in the [[2018]] [[Star Wars Anthology Series|''Star Wars'' Anthology]] film ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', portrayed by [[Woody Harrelson]]. Early fan speculation was that Harrelson would be playing [[Garris Shrike]]—Han Solo's mentor in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity who first appeared in [[A. C. Crispin]]'s ''[[The Han Solo Trilogy]]'' book series—but this was disproved when Harrelson revealed Beckett's name on [[Wikipedia:The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon|''The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon'']].{{WebCite|url=https://comicbook.com/starwars/news/star-wars-who-is-woody-harrelson-playing-in-han-solo|text=Star Wars: Woody Harrelson Reveals Who He's Playing In Han Solo Movie|author=Ridgely, Charlie|date=2017-03-23|archivedate=20200527050014}} According to screenwriters [[Lawrence Kasdan]] and [[Jon Kasdan]], Beckett is based on [[Wikipedia:Long John Silver|Long John Silver]], the main antagonist of [[Wikipedia:Robert Louis Stevenson|Robert Louis Stevenson's]] [[1800s#1883|1883]] novel [[Wikipedia:Treasure Island|''Treasure Island'']].{{WebCite|url=https://ew.com/movies/2018/02/09/solo-a-star-wars-story-woody-harrelson-thandie-newton-paul-bettany|text=''Star Wars'': Woody Harrelson, Thandie Newton, Paul Bettany character details|author=Breznican, Anthony|date=2018-02-09|work=[[Wikipedia:Entertainment Weekly|Entertainment Weekly]]|archivedate=20200527050119}} Beckett's later betrayal was meant to rhyme the moment of [[1977]] [[original trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']] in which Han Solo returns during the [[Battle of Yavin]] to aid [[Luke Skywalker]] in destroying the [[DS-1 Orbital Battle Station|Death Star]], as in both movies, the cynical and older character reluctantly departs and then suddenly returns, though in Beckett's case, it was for betrayal rather than for heroic nature.{{Twitter|JonKasdan|status/1040529511513616385|[[Jon Kasdan]]|quote=continued|archivedate=20181002054217}} Before Harrelson's casting, [[Wikipedia:Christian Bale|Christian Bale]] was in the mix to play Beckett, but despite feeling tempted by the offer due to liking the ''[[Star Wars]]'' franchise since his childhood and having a strong relationship with [[Lucasfilm]] president [[Kathleen Kennedy]] and her husband [[Wikipedia:Frank Marshall (filmmaker)|Frank Marshall]] since [[Steven Spielberg]]'s [[1987]] film [[Wikipedia:Empire of the Sun (film)|''Empire of the Sun'']], Bale didn't take the part though he expressed interest to participate in further discussions.{{WebCite|url=https://collider.com/christian-bale-han-solo-movie-star-wars/|text=Christian Bale Confirms He Was in Talks for a Role in ‘Solo: A Star Wars Story’|author=Chitwood, Adam|date=2018-01-02|work=[[Wikipedia:Collider (website)|Collider]]|archivedate=20190116072446}} Harrelson almost turned down the offer to play Beckett due to wishing to spend more time with his family, but accepted the role upon learning of [[Phoebe Waller-Bridge]]'s casting as [[L3-37]], as he was a fan of Waller-Bridge's ''[[Wikipedia:Fleabag|Fleabag]]'' tragicomedy series.{{WebCite|url=https://metro.co.uk/2018/09/24/woody-harrelson-admits-he-would-have-turned-down-solo-a-star-wars-story-role-if-it-wasnt-for-co-star-7975224/|text=Woody Harrelson admits he would have turned down Solo: A Star Wars Story role if it wasn’t for co-star|author=Akingbade, Toby|date=2018-09-24|work=[[Wikipedia:Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]|archivedate=20210119065542}} Throughout the production of ''Solo'', Beckett's first name was Mattias, as reflected in early printings of ''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' by [[Phil Szostak]].''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' However, the character's name was changed to Tobias late in production; this was corrected for more recent printings of ''The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story''.{{Twitter|PhilSzostak|status/1049778868188409858|[[Phil Szostak]]|quote=Yes, as was Lady Proxima from Mother Proxima. Both have been corrected in more recent printings of The Art of Solo.
